implementation_constraints: Pure Python 3.8+ standard library only (json, sys); no third-party packages
Single file source/impl.py, executed as `python impl.py`, reads all of stdin and always exits 0
No sockets, HTTP parsing, headers, query strings or persistence — routing is done by string matching on the path field
Responses buffered and emitted as one JSON array so a malformed request object can still yield exactly ERROR with nothing else printed
State held in one in-memory Store instance created per run; monotonic id counter never rewound on delete

unresolved_intent.decision: Accept only pure decimal digit strings with value >= 1 (so "+1", " 1", "1.0", "-3", "0" and "01"-style non-canonical forms are all rejected as undefined paths -> 404)
unresolved_intent.rationale: Spec says a non-positive-integer segment yields 404 but does not define the lexical form; strict isdigit plus value>0 is the narrowest reading and keeps the 404-vs-405 boundary deterministic

unresolved_intent.ir_region: trailing slash and empty path segments (e.g. /items/, /items//1)
unresolved_intent.decision: Treated as undefined paths -> 404 {"error":"not found"}, not as /items or /items/1
unresolved_intent.rationale: Only /items and /items/<id> are defined; splitting on / makes a trailing slash an empty final segment that matches no route, avoiding an invented alias

unresolved_intent.ir_region: ordering of 400 (bad body) vs 404 (missing item) on PUT /items/<id>
unresolved_intent.decision: Body validation runs first: a bad body on a nonexistent id returns 400, not 404
unresolved_intent.rationale: The spec lists body validation as a request-shape error independent of resource existence; validating shape before lookup keeps the rule uniform with POST and is the only ordering that makes AC-RH-05 unconditional

unresolved_intent.ir_region: malformed element inside an otherwise valid JSON array (e.g. a string, or an object lacking method/path)
unresolved_intent.decision: Abort the whole run and print exactly ERROR — no partial response array
unresolved_intent.rationale: Spec scopes ERROR to "not a JSON array of request objects", which such input is; the batch-continues rule (AC-RH-05) is explicitly about body errors on well-formed requests, so it does not apply here
